pr_title: [client] Add simple support for gzip compression
pr_body:
Adds a `RestClient.setCompressionEnabled()` setting that will gzip-
compress request bodies and add a `Accept-Encoding: gzip` header so
that the ES server can send compressed responses.

Fixes #62044

issue_context.title: RestClient should allow compressing request bodies
issue_context.body:
The Rest client has transparent support for compressed responses, but no support for compressed requests.

The low-level client should make it easy to compress request bodies, either globally or per-request. The high-level client should automatically benefit from this feature.

Compressing the request body should be driven by adding the corresponding header on `RequestOptions`, e.g.:

```java
RequestOptions gzipOptions = RequestOptions.DEFAULT.toBuilder().addHeader("Content-Encoding", "gzip").build();
esClient.search(new SearchRequest("foo"), gzipOptions);
```

We can also add a more convenient `RequestOption.compress(true)` but ultimately that will set the header option as illustrated above, since that header can always be set directly.
comments:
This would be a great improvement. I spent a few hours today trying to compress request bodies but failed to find a user-level workaround. 

Any user who pay outgoing data transfer should be greatly interested by this feature :dollar:

review_comments: Is this custom encoding needed given the response headers will have the `Content-Encoding` header to be verified in the tests?

Writing the request and response encoding in the response body is meant to allow the test to check what their values are from the server point of view, along with checking that both sides correctly encoded/decoded data if needed (i.e. both server and client were able to read the entity bodies).

Since from the caller's perspective all this is transparent and it receives an unencoded entity, we should expect `Content-Encoding` to be removed.

Testing further, I think the current behavior is buggy. When a gzip-encoded response is received:
* `response.getEntity().getContentEncoding()` is `null` (thanks to `GZIPDecompressingEntity`)
* `response.getHeader("Content-Encoding")` is `gzip`

As the entity presented to the application is no more encoded, both values should be `null`. We should therefore remove the response's `Content-Encoding` header in [`RestClient.convertResponse`](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/847a020e417320f6b1c02b816eda71ce79fe5fae/client/rest/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/client/RestClient.java#L303-L308) where gzipped responses are decoded.

WDYT?

That's a great point @swallez 

Would you like do add that support as part of this PR or open an issue and fix it separately?
Let's focus on request compression in this PR. I've opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/63314 for it.
